title: The Bells Ring Backward
text: At midnight every bell in the city rings at once, and the peals run backward, the last note first. Those who listened too long remember things that have not happened yet.

options.label: Cut the bell ropes, and silence whatever is ringing them.

outcomes.text: The towers stand mute. The quiet is worse than the bells, but it is only quiet.
The ropes are cut. The bells ring anyway, slower, as if something else is pulling.

options.label: Gather the scholars and write down what the bells say, whatever it costs to hear.

outcomes.text: The ink runs out before the bells stop. The pages name next winter's dead, and the Houses read them by candlelight.
The scholar who wrote longest walks into the river at dawn, still writing. A Scion who sat beside him has not slept since.

options.label: Climb the towers and ring them forward again, by hand, until dawn.

outcomes.text: The ringers' hands bleed, but the peals turn the right way round. The city sleeps.
One tower rings the wrong way to the end. The Scion who climbed it comes down at dawn with white hair and a grandfather's hands.
